html:
Conversation navigation and deletion

The controller reads conversation state from its runtime hub. Deletion first records durable intent and hides the selected conversations from normal access; an idle collector then retires their owned state. An HTTP success acknowledges that request. It does not mean every payload or recovery copy has been removed, or that an external operation has stopped.

For individual task retirement, the shared browser observer, detached feedback and task-expiry labels, see task deletion and cleanup feedback flows. That guide separates local request state, accepted removal and observed completion.

Owners and boundaries

Implementation Responsibility
Conversation routes Expose summary, history, metadata, policy, preview, deletion and collection-status APIs; translate known management failures.
ConversationManagementService Project activity and pending cleanup, validate selection models, format previews and choose the RAM or standalone SQL path.
RAM management Inspect shared repository views, revalidate the selection and durably enqueue collection.
Conversation collector Own accepted deletion identities, admission/navigation fences, ownership discovery, cancellation, cleanup and progress.
Deletion journal Persist bounded intent records independently of checkpoint generations.
Abandonment helpers Supply standalone SQL retirement transitions and post-decision cancellation notifications.

The service chooses RAM management when the conversation store exposes its repository records. The standalone SQLite fallback still reserves attached stores and deletes synchronously. Its deleted_count describes that committed deletion; the controller's accepted response has separate collection status. The shared interface does not make the two storage lifecycles identical.

Navigation and history

Search returns cursor pages, normally 50 summaries, with query, sort, status, pinned and task-type filters. The compact index normally returns up to 250 rows. Running-filter membership comes from current execution activity before pagination; it is not inferred from the latest saved turn's status. An optional bulk activity projection can be omitted if its lookup fails, with the failure logged.

Metadata and timing endpoints avoid loading the full transcript. The turn-window endpoint normally returns 12 turns and accepts before, after, through and around anchors, exclusions and submitted/latest-reply ordering. Routes add task lineage, admission and approved-plan projections from their owners; saved chat rows remain request-scoped. The legacy whole-conversation endpoint still includes debug detail by default, so it is not the bounded navigation interface.

For pending deletion, management clears preview text and active-run decorations and adds the collector's gc status. A compact locked summary can remain visible after the live chat row has gone, until recovery-copy cleanup finishes. These extra rows appear only on the first page, respect title/pin filtering and are not inserted into status/task-type filtered results. Opening a hidden conversation can therefore return 404 while its cleanup row is still visible.

Selection, preview and confirmation

A selection contains either explicit conversation IDs or all_matching with optional filters and exclusions. The model rejects combining the two modes. Explicit IDs and exclusion lists each allow at most 1,000 entries; search text is limited to 256 characters. Missing explicit IDs do not become candidates.

Preview examines queued prompts, tasks and attempts, lanes, pending steering, native runs and continuations, jobs, unresolved receipts/owners, schedules and monitors. It returns blocker counts and two digests:

  • selection_digest binds the complete sorted set of existing selected IDs.
  • safety_digest binds the inspected content and work facts used by protected deletion.

The detailed conversation/blocked lists are capped at 100 rows and each displayed blocker list at 20 entries. The digests and counts cover the full selection despite that display limit. They compare review freshness; they are not authorization tokens and do not reserve the selection.

Protected deletion rechecks safety and requires explicit acknowledgement before discarding never-started queued chat tasks. Bulk deletion can accept unblocked members while returning blocked members. Legacy single/clear endpoints require the whole selection to be eligible. Known conflicts return HTTP 409; invalid inputs return 422 and missing route identities generally return 404.

Explicit abandonment requires both preview digests in the request, but compares the selected identities rather than requiring unchanged work. The RAM acceptance path does not traverse all execution history again for this mode. A change in the selected set requires another review; work progressing inside that same set does not. Ownership discovery and retirement belong to the collector.

Durable acceptance and eventual cleanup

sequenceDiagram participant UI as Conversation UI participant API as Routes and management participant Hub as Runtime hub participant Journal as Deletion journal participant GC as Idle collector UI->>API: Preview selected conversations API-->>UI: Identities, blockers and digests UI->>API: Confirm reviewed selection API->>Hub: Atomic read-only revalidation Hub-->>API: Accepted identities and compact summaries API->>Journal: Write intent, fsync, replace, sync directory API->>GC: Install fences and wake collector API-->>UI: accepted_ids, deletion_ids and gc status GC->>Hub: Discover ownership and collect when eligible GC->>Journal: Persist cleanup progress UI->>API: Read collection status API-->>UI: Current phase and completion facts

One acceptance lock serializes intent publication. Journal I/O happens outside hub/task locks; a read-only hub transaction does not itself perform the filesystem commit. The journal writes a private temporary file, fsyncs it, replaces the final identity file and syncs its directory. Records are bounded to 16 MiB and validated on load; malformed records fail closed. An unacknowledged temporary file is not an accepted deletion.

Retrying explicit IDs already owned by one collection returns that collection. Overlapping selections retain their existing durable owners; only newly selected identities receive a new intent. This avoids rewriting an in-progress purge. Recovery reloads durable intent so restoring an older checkpoint does not expose a conversation that was already accepted for deletion.

The RAM response reports accepted_count, accepted_ids, per-conversation deletion_ids, collection records and optional fallback navigation. It reports zero deleted_count/deleted_turns and leaves evidence_retained unset (null) at acceptance. Clients must use collection status for actual progress. A single deletion's fallback is the nearest older conversation by chronology, independent of pinning or the active search order.

Status separates the durable state from a display phase: queued, cleaning, waiting for a checkpoint/save, purging disk copies, paused for active tasks, retrying, or complete. RAM cleanup alone does not establish disk completion. Active tasks can delay cleanup, and new work can pause collection between batches. The journal and collector retain progress across interruption; acceptance does not hold an HTTP request open until collection finishes.

External effects, resources and policy scope

Cancellation notifications use existing local events and Gateway cancellation owners. Transport failures are logged; an unreachable Gateway is not proof that a remote job stopped. Late settlement and unresolved execution evidence keep their existing ownership. Independent schedules, monitors and task objects are not simply cascaded away with a conversation.

Attachment grants, body files, task scratch data, private sessions and persisted recovery copies have separate owners. Acceptance installs access/admission fences; eventual removal follows those owners' shared-reference and evidence-retention rules. See artifacts and context and state and recovery.

The same route group exposes permission and capability previews/edits. Authorities own inheritance, validation and optional expected-revision checks. A saved-request permission preview resolves its accepted resume context; a draft conversation override is valid only without an existing conversation/request identity. Capability catalog availability is editor metadata, not an execution grant. Policy edits publish notifications after saving, and notification errors can propagate after the save. Management deletion notifications, in contrast, are best effort after durable acceptance; neither path rolls back a committed decision because an observer failed.

Verification references

Management fixtures exercise selection, search, blockers, strict routes and standalone behavior. RAM management fixtures cover shared-owner transactions and retained evidence. Asynchronous deletion fixtures cover acknowledgement without collection, idle admission, restart recovery, settlement and progress phases. These tests use isolated state; they do not prove that a real external operation can always be cancelled.
